about: CHAIN sword_smuggle (Design/content/chains/sword_smuggle.md): Frankish swords going north against the king's bans, 795 to about 812. Thirteen cards. The spine's thread swords_north. A smith of Colonia (Reginbald, invented) has blades the count never counted; the count's man searches the boat at Dorestad; the crew have their say at sea; a dealer on the Slie (the spine's cast.asulf) buys for weighed silver or for captives; a second, bigger cargo goes north in a wine cask past the watch boat at the river mouth; a lord of the Danes asks for the smith himself; and then, on a Frisian landing, a blade with the smith's mark comes back in a dead man. Four endings: the runner (what really happened: the blades went north all the same), the king's finder (the hard road, with the finder's share of Thionville 805), the smith carried north (history changed: flag changed_frankish_smith_north), and the blade laid down at Saint Martin's. Progress is flags ch_sword_smuggle_1 to _9; the spine's flags sw_ran_blades, sw_marked and sw_buyer_known are set where their meaning is met. Scheduled cards have weight 0 and are reached only by 'schedule' (their 'when' says when they belong; the scheduler does not read it). The words are in Data/writing/chain_sword_smuggle.json; each option's note names the writing key of its outcome text (the engine shows the effects' own facts; the outcome keys are for the integrator). Law: capitularies of Herstal 779, of 803, of Thionville 805 and of Boulogne 811, as in chronicle_793.json. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start (drawn at Colonia from 795 once the house has 120 d aboard). Reginbald the smith (invented: Regin- + -bald) has four blades the count's man never counted. Sources: Herstal 779 c. 20, no byrnie sold out of the realm (MGH Capit. I no. 20); the missi's capitulary of 803, no arm-rings or byrnies to merchants (chronicle_793.json 803-arms-to-merchants-803); Thionville 805 c. 7 (805-12-thionville-border-posts); swords made in the Rhineland and wanted in the north (goods_793.json swords; dossiers/colonia.md). The mark of a hammer in a ring is ours; inlaid marks on blades of the time are known (?). The name in the iron is the +VLFBERH+T inlay, from about 800 (Wikipedia 'Ulfberht swords'); who he was and where he worked is not known (?). Sets ch_sword_smuggle_1 and one of ch_sword_smuggle_carrying, ch_sword_smuggle_clean.

cards.note: Step 3 (a crew card, drawn under way while the first blades are aboard; it is passed over if the boat reaches the buyer first). The spine's hook for the crew: Ravn (cast.crew.ravn) says the Franks made the law because they fear the edge; Aldger (cast.crew.aldger) will not row a cargo that can hang him; Brunger (cast.crew.brunger), a Saxon baptised by the sword, would arm anyone the king calls an enemy. The lines are true of them and harmless in other mouths. The riddle is the Gestumblindi riddle of the smith's bellows (riddles_793.json r-gest-09), where 'wound-leek' is a sword. Sets ch_sword_smuggle_3.

cards.note: Step 4 (drawn at Sliesthorp or Ripa after the search; a turn). The buyer: Asulf (cast.asulf), a dealer in captives who would rather have blades than silver. Sources: the spine's hook for Sliesthorp (a Dane pays double in weighed silver; Asulf pays in captives); silver by weight north of the Eider, no coin before about 825 (BRIEF.md rule 2); Anskar bought Danish and Slav boys (Rimbert c. 15, tr. Robinson 1921); Godfred moved the merchants of Reric to Sliesthorp in 808 (Annales regni Francorum 808; chronicle 808-summer-reric-destroyed). Four ounces the blade is the game's price: about 65 d, a blade without its hilt at the forge being 45 d; the ounce (eyrir) of about 27 g is the later Norse weight (?). Sets ch_sword_smuggle_4, the spine's sw_buyer_known, and the timer ch_sword_smuggle_rest (40 days).

cards.note: Step 5 (drawn at Colonia from 40 days after step 4). The smith has a wine cask with no wine in it: eight blades in straw and tallow, as the big houses send them (the spine: Thiadbod sends blades north in wine casks and has never been caught). He warns of the watch boat at the river mouth: every danger warns first. His journeyman Hrodwin (invented: Hrod- + -win) asks what a smith is worth in the north. Sources: Thionville 805 c. 6, a byrnie for every man with twelve manses, so the lords take all the mail there is (chronicle 805-12-thionville-arms); Boulogne 811, churches not to give or sell byrnies or swords to outsiders (811-10-boulogne-capitulary); Charles had ships built and watches set at the river mouths from 800 (Einhard, Vita Karoli c. 17). Sets ch_sword_smuggle_5 and one of ch_sword_smuggle_carrying with ch_sword_smuggle_big, ch_sword_smuggle_tools, ch_sword_smuggle_boy_asked.

cards.note: Step 7 (drawn at Sliesthorp after the watch boat; a turn). Asulf has a guest who buys for a lord with many ships: before 804 no lord is named (Sigfred is king of the Danes in the Frankish annals to 798 and little more than a name: realms/denmark.md); from 804 he is King Godfred's man (cast.godfred, first named in 804, killed 810: chronicle 804-summer-godfred-sliesthorp). The offer for the smith himself is ours; that the north wanted the makers as well as the blades is shown by blades with the Frankish name inlaid wrongly, held to be copies made outside the Rhineland (Wikipedia 'Ulfberht swords') (?). Notker's tale of Northmen's envoys and the testing of swords (De Carolo Magno II.18, tr. Grant 1907) stands behind the spokesman's line and is not quoted (?). Sets ch_sword_smuggle_7, ch_sword_smuggle_offer, and the timer ch_sword_smuggle_wait (120 days).

cards.note: Step 8 (drawn at a Frisian landing, or at Traiectum or Dorestad where the boat is brought up the river, from 120 days after step 7): the day a sold blade comes back. Folcbod (invented: Folc- + -bod), who set eel traps in the outer channels, lies dead in his boat with a Frankish blade left in him; it carries the smith's mark. His widow Liafburg (Liaf- + -burg) and his son Eilger (Eil- + -ger) stand by. Sources: in 810 a fleet of two hundred ships from the land of the Northmen came to Frisia, ravaged the islands, beat the Frisians in three fights and took a hundred pounds of silver as tribute (Annales regni Francorum 810; chronicle 810-summer-frisia-raid-810): the year line of 810 says so in our own words. Sea robbery on the Frisian coast before 810 is not recorded and is ours (?). The spine: 'a blade sold in 800 can come back'. Sets ch_sword_smuggle_8 and one of ch_sword_smuggle_told (with ch_sword_smuggle_paid_widow), ch_sword_smuggle_silent.

cards.note: ENDING 'runner' (scheduled 60 days after step 9, at Sliesthorp): what really happened. The bans did not hold: about 170 blades with the Frankish name inlaid lie in the north and east, most of them in Norway, Sweden, the Baltic lands and Rus (Wikipedia 'Ulfberht swords'), and the law had to be made again in 811 and, with death for it, in 864 (chronicle 864-06-25-pitres). The guest-right of a foreign merchant under a lord's protection and a plot by the water are as at the trading places of the north (the plots of Ribe and Hedeby were laid out in rows; from memory (?)). Sets ch_sword_smuggle_end_runner; grand reward unlock_plot_sliesthorp or unlock_title_danish_guest_right; the lasting cost ch_sword_smuggle_blood_owed (the dead man's kin know whose cargo it was) and, with the plot, the spine's sw_marked.

cards.note: ENDING 'kings_man' (scheduled 40 days after step 9, at Dorestad): the hard road, and the richest. The count's court; the road is closed for a season. Sources: Thionville 805 c. 7, half of the seized goods to the palace and half shared between the officer and the finder (MGH Capit. I no. 44): before 805 the reward is the king's grace, which is ours (?). The king's protection for merchants: Louis the Pious's letter for merchants of the palace, 828, freeing them of toll everywhere but Quentovic, Dorestad and the passes (Formulae imperiales no. 37; from memory (?)): a toll charter for Dorestad itself is a grant beyond it, and ours. A smith made a man of the palace is as the smiths of the royal estates (Capitulare de villis c. 45) (?). The big house (cast.thiadbod) is not touched: chain house_rival owns his fate. Sets ch_sword_smuggle_end_kings_man; grand rewards unlock_title_kings_protection and unlock_charter_dorestad; the lasting cost ch_sword_smuggle_dane_enmity.

cards.note: ENDING 'smith_north' (scheduled 45 days after step 9, at Sliesthorp): HISTORY CHANGED. A Rhineland master forges on the Slie with his own mark, a lifetime before the north made such blades for itself. What is true: the Frankish blades were made in the Rhineland and only hilted in the north (goods_793.json sword_blades); blades with the name inlaid wrongly are held to be later copies (Wikipedia 'Ulfberht swords') (?). No Frankish smith is recorded going north; the house by the water, the iron and the charcoal are the spokesman's offer of step 7. Sets changed_frankish_smith_north and ch_sword_smuggle_end_smith_north; grand reward unlock_work_sliesthorp_forge with unlock_factor_sliesthorp, or unlock_heirloom_first_northern_blade; the lasting cost is the spine's sw_marked and ch_sword_smuggle_rhine_watched (the palace has the house's name).

cards.note: ENDING 'laid_down' (scheduled 30 days after step 9, at Traiectum): the blade is given to Saint Martin and the house takes the saint's side of the river. Sources: Saint Martin's church at Utrecht (Traiectum) and its men on the banks at Dorestad, who owe the king's officers nothing: Louis the Pious for Utrecht, 18 March 815, confirming older grants (Oorkondenboek Sticht Utrecht I no. 56, in dossiers/dorestad.md); that it held before 815 is assumed (?). Fostering a dead man's son is the custom of every people of this coast. Iron given to a church and worked into its door is ours. A free man who gives himself to a saint for a yearly due of wax is a Carolingian institution (from memory (?)). Sets ch_sword_smuggle_end_laid_down; grand rewards unlock_title_st_martins_man and, if the boy is taken aboard, unlock_kin_fosterling_eilger.
